messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Alert triggered for redwood-prod-1 — KV cache cardinality growing rapidly, continuous-batching latency cliff, error rate +5x over baseline. Severity: P1. Pager routed to @ben_oncall. Logs: https://logs.redwood/in/abcdef

ben_oncall: seeing same. Observed a spike in token latency and OOMs on the batching worker. Prefetch/kv cache size jumped from ~1.2M keys to 18M in ~8m. impact: streaming latency >2s for some routes, 502s on a few requests.

ben_oncall: quick triage commands i'm running:
```
# top offending keys by prefix size (redis sample)
redis-cli -h kv-prod-01 --scan --pattern \"prefix:*\" | xargs -n1 redis-cli -h kv-prod-01 memory usage | sort -nr | head -n 20
# check continuous-batcher tail logs
kubectl -n prod logs continuous-batcher-0 -c batch-runner --since=15m | grep \"evict\"
```

alice.prod: I can confirm template-driven prompts look to be generating slightly different template hashes; multiple customers hitting slightly different prefixes. suspiciously tokenization mismatch after recent tokenizer update.

chandra_ml: pulling model-side diffs now. We shipped a small tokenizer normalization change yesterday to reduce whitespace variance. hypothesis: normalization changed token counts for some templates and invalidated prompt-hash deduping, creating many unique cache keys.

dave_sre: good catch. If cache keys are exploding, we should stop continuous batching and evict pathological prefixes while we patch. Can we flip the batch config to conservative mode?

ben_oncall: patching batch config to reduce max_batch_size and disable prefix-prefetch for now. applying hotfix:
```
# apply config change via ops-api
curl -X POST https://ops-api.redwood/configs/batcher -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPTS_TOKEN' -d '{"max_batch_size":8, "prefix_prefetch":false, "kv_eviction_threshold":0.6}'
```

incident-bot: Deploy started by ben_oncall — rollout to continuous-batcher pool (3/3 nodes)

maria_support: flagging affected customers: cs-team, start customer comms if SLOs impacted. I ran queries and saw elevated latencies for orgs org-123, org-789.

ben_oncall: while rollout in-flight, I'm running targeted eviction for the largest prefixes to reclaim memory without full cluster eviction:
```
# list top prefixes and evict up to 500k keys per prefix
redis-cli -h kv-prod-01 --scan --pattern \"prefix:template-*\" | sed -n '1,500000p' | xargs -n1 redis-cli -h kv-prod-01 del
```

alice.prod: warning: evicting live prefixes may increase tail latency temporarily as model re-computes prefixes. but better than sustained OOMs.

dave_sre: roll complete. batcher config now conservative on all pods. observed immediate drop in memory growth rate. continuing eviction passes.

chandra_ml: dug into tokenizer change: commit 7f3a2d — normalizes zero-width joiners and collapses certain punctuation sequences. For 12 prompt templates we saw tokenization shift cause distinct prompt-hash generation — previously mapped to 1 canonical key, now split into dozens. Fix path options:
- rollback tokenizer normalizer
- add backward-compatible hash shim that normalizes old variants
- de-dupe at prefix layer for X minutes

ben_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) keep batch conservative 2) run prefix de-dupe shim (fast) 3) schedule tokenizer rollback if needed. Implementing shim now as config-layer filter that canonicalizes templates to old normalization for 1h.

dave_sre: implementing shim via nginx lua filter on the ingestion path. quick patch applied. logs look cleaner.

incident-bot: Action taken: config hotfix applied, prefix de-dupe shim enabled, targeted eviction completed. Next: monitor 30m for regression.

maria_support: customer impact roundup: about 14 orgs saw degraded latency during window, 3 experienced request failures. CS notified, temporary credits in discussion.

alice.prod: follow-up: we need a prompt-regression test against tokenizer changes in CI — add unit tests that assert stable prompt-hash output for known templates. filing PR to infra-tests.

chandra_ml: added acceptance test vector and a pre-merge gate. also creating migration script to convert newly split prefixes back into canonical keys where safe.

ben_oncall: handing off to dave_sre for monitoring and postmortem. I'll update the incident doc with timeline + commands run. @dave_sre take point for post-incident review.

dave_sre: ack taking over. I'll keep this thread open for 1h and then start a postmortem doc template. preliminary RCA: tokenizer normalization change -> prompt-hash divergence -> prefix cardinality explosion -> KV inertial growth + continuous-batching trying to prefetch -> memory spike -> latency cliff.

ben_oncall: final notes: hotfix rollback plan ready if shim causes regressions. tagging incident as P1 -> reduced to P2 after successful mitigation.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: mitigated. follow-up: postmortem required, assign chandra_ml (cause/patch), dave_sre (ops timeline), alice.prod (testing + CI gate), maria_support (customer comms).

maria_support: drafting customer communication template now, will sync with legal for wording.

alice.prod: thanks all. quick checklist for postmortem:
- timeline with commands run
- metrics (kv-cardinality, latency, error-rate) pre/post
- root cause + change that triggered it
- immediate fix + permanent fix plan
- customer impact table and communications

dave_sre: starting postmortem doc and will ping for review in #incidents-retros. closing on-call handover: ben_oncall -> dave_sre at 1825550900.

ben_oncall: signing off. :thumbsup:
